description: Validates environment variable schemas for type safety, unique names, typed defaults, secret hygiene, and operational accountability

rules.description: env-schema-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare a non-empty envKeys array and an unknownKeyPolicy. Every key must have a name and a recognised type
No two entries in envKeys may share the same name. Duplicate env var names cause silent runtime ambiguity — the last declaration wins and the schema contract becomes unreliable

Every env key must declare a recognised type and must explicitly declare either required: true or a default value. A key with neither is ambiguous — the runtime cannot know how to behave when the variable is absent

constraints.optionality: Each key must have required: true OR a default value — neither is rejected as ambiguous

rules.description: Default values must conform to the key's declared type. A default that fails its own type rule is a silent spec-time bug — the validator rejects it at startup with no warning at authoring time
rules.note: Skipped for keys that have no default value

rules.description: Keys marked secret: true must not have a literal default value in the spec, and must not have a literal value committed in any .env file (excluding .env.example). A secret with a literal default is a hardcoded credential that will appear in source control and container image layers
rules.note: Skipped when no keys declare secret: true

rules.description: env-schema-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers

Every env key must have a non-empty description (undescribed keys are opaque to operators during incidents). Required keys must not declare a default value — a required key with a default is self-contradicting and causes inconsistent validator behaviour at runtime

constraints.description: All keys must declare a non-empty description string
constraints.required-no-default: Keys with required: true must not also declare a default value
